explanations: The close handler only removes the client from the clients map. Its client id stays in every per-trip subscriber set it joined (client.trips is never used to clean up), and the trip entry stays in subscribers. For trips that never call endTrip (cancelled, abandoned, gateway restarts of the trip service), the sets grow forever, and every publish iterates dead ids. It is a slow memory leak and the stats() subscriptions count drifts upward. Closing should iterate client.trips and call unsubscribe for each.

publish checks bufferedAmount > MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES (256 KB) and, if exceeded, increments dropped and continues. It does not terminate or throw, and the frame is never sent to that socket, so it is not queued.

Driver positions are snapshots: the next frame fully replaces the last, so dropping intermediate ones loses nothing essential and protects server memory. ws does not redeliver skipped frames, riders do not resend anything, and nothing in the code retries publish.

JSON.stringify runs once and the same string is sent to every subscriber, so cost per extra rider is just the send. It has nothing to do with ordering across trips, Node has a single JS thread here, and slow sockets are handled by the bufferedAmount check, not serialization.
